summary: Harden L1–L5 workflow checkpoint reliability with resume-from-checkpoint, add structured error classification with typed SSE events, complete Knowledge CRUD (delete, rename fix, type-specific fields), and improve memory retrieval precision with story-scope filtering and relevance ranking.
approach: Three-wave execution. Wave 1: backend changes (checkpoint resume logic, error classification, retrieval scoring) — all parallel since they touch different modules. Wave 2: frontend changes (error recovery UI, knowledge CRUD) — depend on Wave 1 backend APIs. Wave 3: tests for all Phase 2 changes.
design_decisions: Checkpoint resume uses existing runtime-state.js step status tracking — no new persistence layer needed
Error classification adds a typed `error_class` field to SSE events in responses.js — backward compatible (missing field = unknown)
Knowledge delete uses graph-engine.js `deleteEntity(name)` which already cascades to relations — frontend just needs UI + Cypher DELETE
Rename fix: change PersistedEntityTab to use separate MATCH + SET instead of MERGE when matchName differs from draftName
Memory retrieval uses TF-IDF token overlap scoring on top of existing FTS5 — no vector DB needed

patterns: SSE events follow the shape builders in responses.js — new error types must add builder functions
Knowledge CRUD uses `buildGraphMergeMutation()` from knowledgeUtils.ts — delete needs new `buildGraphDeleteMutation()`
Frontend hooks follow the pattern: useState + useCallback + side-effect in useEffect
conventions: Backend sidecar uses plain JS with JSDoc comments, no TypeScript
Frontend uses React hooks + Zustand stores, no class components
All graph mutations go through graph-engine.js `executeCypher()` or direct methods
dependencies: graph-engine.js deleteEntity() already exists — just not wired to frontend
runtime-state.js step status machine already tracks completed steps — resume flag is additive
